title: CHATCOM normalized message
description: One chat message after ingest. Every adapter (WhatsApp, Telegram, transcripts, screenshots; later Messenger, Instagram, GroupMe, iMessage) writes this shape, one JSON object per line. System lines (joins, subject changes, the encryption notice) are not messages and never appear here.

id.description: Keyed hash (HMAC-SHA256 with the show's secret, 16 hex). exact/minute rows: (raw label, UTC minute, ordinal within label-minute, identity text). day/order rows: (raw label, day, identity text, previous row's label and identity text, run ordinal). Stable across re-exports and overlapping imports of the same chat.

sender.description: Display name after aliases and --speaker. A sender shown only as a phone number is masked ('Unnamed 1a2b3c') until the operator sets an alias.

time.description: ISO 8601 with the show's UTC offset. For day and order rows the time is synthetic: strictly increasing in chat order, anchored to the date the source shows.

time_precision.description: How much of `time` the source really showed: exact (seconds or better), minute, day (a date, no time) or order (no date).

text.description: Normalized text: NFC, invisible direction marks removed, the 'edited' marker removed. Empty for a media-only or deleted message.

media.description: Kind of attachment when the export replaced it with a placeholder. CHATCOM never reads media files.

reply_to.description: id of the message this one replies to, when the source carries it (Telegram). Null otherwise.

sender.description: Null when the source shows only a count, as screenshots do.

reactions.description: Null when the source does not carry reactions (WhatsApp .txt).

label.description: The sender exactly as the source showed it, before aliases (a phone number is replaced by its label). Ids use it, so renaming never changes an id.

line.description: First line of the message in a text export.

image.description: Screenshot copy the row came from.

quote.description: A quoted reply as the source shows it. Exclusion removes quotes by excluded senders.
